claims.text: The target alloy is a Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy derived from the Cantor alloy.
Grain boundary engineering can improve the balance of strength and ductility of Co-free FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.
Grain boundary engineering can produce a more stable grain boundary structure.
A more stable grain boundary structure improves both strength and ductility under dynamic loading.
Tailored microstructures can improve mechanical properties in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed improvement is valid from -200°C to 500°C.
The proposed improvement is valid at strain rates from 10^-3/s to 10^3/s.
The exact grain boundary engineering technique is unknown.
The optimal processing parameters for the proposed intervention are unknown.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis refers to introducing a specific grain boundary engineering technique, but the intervention names only the broad category of grain boundary engineering and the uncertainty field states that the exact technique is unknown.
The conditions characterize the loading as dynamic, whereas the stated validity range extends down to 10^-3/s, which is ordinarily a quasi-static strain rate.
